title: A lazy part whose chunk failed to load never loads again on "Try again"
body:
## Summary
lib/lazy.ts lazyPart builds one React.lazy at creation; once a render-time load rejects, React keeps that rejection, so every later draw of the part (a boundary's "Try again") rethrows the old error.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/lazy.ts:25-35 resets `pending` on rejection and its comments (lazy.ts:27, :40) say a failed fetch is retried by the next render, but `Suspending = lazy(preload)` (lazy.ts:34) is created once and React.lazy caches a rejected payload for good. 14 parts use lazyPart; apps/desktop/client/src/shared/boundary/ErrorBoundary.tsx:46 offers "Try again", which redraws the same rejected lazy. Measured fix trap: swapping in a fresh lazy inside the rejection handler makes React's own error-recovery re-render load again and again - with a permanently failing load the instrument test hung to its 5 s timeout. A correct fix renews only on a NEW attempt (boundary reset), e.g. ErrorBoundary onRetry -> part.preload(), or a key-scoped renewal; that seam crosses lib/lazy.ts and shared/boundary (another round's file), hence M.

## Flow
- instrument: the test saved at scratchpad/lazy.test.instrument.tsx (a Catch boundary keyed 1 then 2; load fails while offline, then succeeds) - red at HEAD ('failed' instead of 'hello back')
- renew the lazy only on a new attempt (ErrorBoundary onRetry or a key-scoped renewal), never inside React's retry of the same render
- assert a permanently failing load stays bounded (load calls per attempt <= 3) and the retry draws the part

## Expected impact
An owner whose module page failed to load once (dev server restart, a stale chunk after an update) recovers with "Try again" instead of reloading the window. Risk: a naive renewal loops the loader while offline - the bounded-call assertion guards it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - "Try again" after a failed chunk load draws the part
Before: instrument test red at HEAD: after a failed render the redraw shows 'failed', load not called again
After: naive fix (new lazy on rejection): retry works but a permanent failure loops (test timed out at 5004 ms); bounded fix not built
Method: probe - test built and run on HEAD and on one candidate fix; the bounded fix needs the boundary seam outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scratchpad/lazy.test.instrument.tsx case "loads the chunk again when the part is drawn again" plus a bounded-load-count assertion for a permanently failing load

title: Bump vite 8.3.2 to >=8.3.4: six advisories, one high, on the Windows dev server
body:
## Summary
pnpm audit reports 6 advisories (1 high, 4 moderate, 1 low) in vite 8.3.2, all patched in 8.3.3; nine other dependencies trail by a patch release.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/package.json:32 pins vite ^8.3.2 and apps/desktop/client/pnpm-lock.yaml resolves 8.3.2. `pnpm --dir apps/desktop/client audit` (2026-10-22): high "launch-editor: fs.existsSync() existence check can be bypassed on Windows"; moderate x4 (launch-editor % escaping on Windows, editor CLI flag misinterpretation, files outside server.fs.allow served, first 4 bytes of files outside server.fs via ?vite-wasm-instance); low (cross-origin script execution through custom middleware). Patched >=8.3.3; latest 8.3.4. The project develops on Windows and apps/desktop/client/vite.config.ts:20 sets server.fs.allow to the repository root. `pnpm outdated` also lists patch bumps: @tanstack/react-query 5.104.5, @tanstack/react-virtual 3.14.21, @tauri-apps/api 2.12.4, react/react-dom 19.3.1, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2, jsdom 30.1.3, vitest 5.0.5, @types/node 26.6.5. vite is dev-only (the shipped bundle is static files), so the exposure is the developer machine.

## Flow
- pnpm --dir apps/desktop/client up vite@^8.3.4 (lockfile + package.json), optionally the patch set above in the same change
- run the full gate: typecheck, full vitest run, pnpm build (the director's gate)
- re-run pnpm audit

## Expected impact
Developers running `pnpm dev` on Windows are no longer exposed to the launch-editor and fs.allow bypasses. Risk: a patch release changing build output; the full build gate sees it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - known advisories in the client toolchain go to zero
Before: pnpm audit: 6 vulnerabilities (1 high, 4 moderate, 1 low), all vite 8.3.2; pnpm outdated: 10 packages one patch behind
After: predicted: pnpm audit 0 (every advisory patched >=8.3.3)
Method: simulation - the bump changes the lockfile and needs pnpm install plus the full gate (pnpm build), which the brief reserves for the director
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: pnpm --dir apps/desktop/client audit (6 -> 0) plus the full client gate (typecheck, vitest run, pnpm build) green

title: The client has no dependency-advisory gate while Rust has cargo-deny
body:
## Summary
CI checks RustSec advisories through cargo-deny on every push, but nothing runs pnpm audit for the client, so the 6 vite advisories were found by hand.

## Description
.github/workflows/ci.yml:25-32 runs cargo-deny `check` (advisories included; the AGENTS.md dependency gate); the client job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:6-24) runs install, typecheck, test and build only. docs/build/STATUS.md:2175 lists "the dependency licences and pnpm audit" as not checked. One dependency policy, two ecosystems, one gated. Fixed: a client step `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` after install, landed after the vite bump card so it starts green.

## Flow
- land the vite bump card first (audit exit 1 -> 0)
- add `- run: pnpm audit --audit-level=high` to the client job in .github/workflows/ci.yml
- seed: re-pin vite 8.3.2 on a branch and watch the step fail

## Expected impact
A high advisory in a client dependency fails CI the way a RustSec advisory already does. Risk: audit reads the advisory feed in CI and a fresh advisory can redden an unrelated push - the same trade cargo-deny already makes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - client dependency advisories are gated like Rust ones
Before: ci.yml: 1 advisory gate (cargo-deny), 0 for the client; pnpm audit today exit 1
After: predicted: 2 gates; the client step exits 0 after the vite bump, 1 on a seeded 8.3.2
Method: simulation - the change lives in .github/workflows/ci.yml, outside this round's paths, and only a CI run executes it
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:25-32 deny job (cargo-deny-action, command: check)
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21-24 client job: install, typecheck, test, build - no audit
docs/build/STATUS.md:2175 "Not checked. ... the dependency licences and `pnpm audit`."
instrument: CI client job with `pnpm audit --audit-level=high`: exit 0 on the bumped tree, exit 1 with vite re-pinned to 8.3.2

title: CI installs and builds the client three times per push
body:
## Summary
The client job and both legs of the rust matrix each run pnpm install and pnpm build for apps/desktop/client.

## Description
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21,24 (client job) and :51-52 in the rust job, whose matrix (:38) runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest: 3 `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and 3 `pnpm build` (each a full tsc + vite build) per push. The rust legs need only dist/ to embed. Fixed: the client job uploads dist/ as an artifact and the rust legs `needs: client` and download it (or the Windows leg keeps its own build if the embed must differ per OS - to be measured).

## Flow
- client job: actions/upload-artifact dist/
- rust job: needs client; actions/download-artifact into apps/desktop/client/dist; drop its install+build steps
- compare CI wall time and runner minutes over two pushes before/after

## Expected impact
Fewer runner minutes and a shorter rust leg on every push. Risk: the rust legs now wait for the client job, so wall time can grow while minutes fall - measure both.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer duplicate client builds in CI
Before: 3 installs + 3 builds of the client per push (ci.yml:21,24 and :51,52 x a matrix of 2)
After: predicted 1 install + 1 build; wall time not measured
Method: simulation - only CI runs can time it and the file is outside this round's paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21 - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
.github/workflows/ci.yml:24 - run: pnpm build
.github/workflows/ci.yml:38 os: [windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]
.github/workflows/ci.yml:51-52 pnpm --dir apps/desktop/client install / build
instrument: two CI runs before and after: total runner minutes and end-to-end wall time

title: A window whose backend fails to start stays blank with an unhandled rejection
body:
## Summary
mount() awaits initBackend with no catch and the three entries call it with `void`, so a failed start (the browser mock chunk missing) leaves an empty page and nothing on screen.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/mount.tsx:18 `await initBackend(label)` then render; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/{main,tumbler,approval}/entry.tsx call `void mount(...)`. apps/desktop/client/src/lib/runtime.ts:84 rethrows a mock load failure outside the desktop app by design (demo.test.ts 'a browser load error is not hidden'), but not hidden currently means a console rejection on a blank page: the director's frames and `pnpm dev` show white. Fixed: mount catches, renders one plain sentence from lib/words.ts into #root (no provider needed) and still logs the error.

## Flow
- browser preview -> mock chunk 404 -> initBackend rejects -> mount rejects -> void -> blank page
- fix: try/await initBackend; on failure write a words.ts sentence into #root and console.error
- test: mount with a rejecting loadMock seam -> #root has the sentence

## Expected impact
A judge opening the browser preview on a broken deploy sees why instead of a white page. Risk: low; the desktop live path cannot reach it (tauriBackend is synchronous).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed start is shown, not blank
Before: failed initBackend -> #root empty, 1 unhandled rejection (3 entries, `void mount`)
After: predicted: #root shows one sentence, 0 unhandled
Method: simulation - the sentence must come from lib/words.ts (shared surface) and mount needs a loader seam; three walked cases (main, tumbler, approval entries)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a mount test with a rejecting mock loader: #root text non-empty and no unhandled rejection

title: Narrow the dev server's fs.allow from the repository root to the client and bindings
body:
## Summary
vite.config.ts lets `pnpm dev` serve any file under the repository root through /@fs/, though the client reads only its own tree and bindings/.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/vite.config.ts:20 `fs: { allow: [here('../../..')] }` - the whole paypal/ tree (docs, .research, crates, .build, target, .claude). Every non-relative import in apps/desktop/client/src is a package or @bindings (vite.config.ts:16); nothing else outside the client is read. With the vite fs.allow-bypass advisories open (see the vite bump card) the allow list is the remaining fence. Fixed: `allow: [here('.'), here('../../../bindings')]` (policy-tighten: serves less).

## Flow
- edit vite.config.ts:20
- start `pnpm dev`; GET /@fs/<repo>/AGENTS.md -> 200 before, 403 after
- open index.html, tumbler.html, approval.html, director.html: each loads (bindings still served)

## Expected impact
The dev server stops serving files the client never needs. Risk: an import from outside client/bindings would 403 in dev only - the four-page smoke catches it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the dev server serves only what the client imports
Before: fs.allow = repository root (one entry covering every tracked and build file)
After: predicted: client + bindings only; /@fs/<repo>/AGENTS.md 403
Method: simulation - verifying needs a running dev server, which the brief forbids round agents
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/vite.config.ts:20 server: { port: 1430, strictPort: true, fs: { allow: [here('../../..')] } }
non-relative imports in apps/desktop/client/src: @bindings, react, @tanstack, @tauri-apps, @testing-library, vitest, node: only
instrument: pnpm dev then GET /@fs/<repo>/AGENTS.md (200 -> 403) and the four pages load

title: The inspector is switched by two env flags that must be set together
body:
## Summary
The Babel stamps follow THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR and the overlay follows VITE_INSPECTOR; only scripts/dev/tauri-dev-test.mjs sets both.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/scripts/babel/source-loc-vite-plugin.mjs:9 reads process.env.THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR; apps/desktop/client/src/lib/mount.tsx:13 reads import.meta.env.VITE_INSPECTOR; scripts/dev/tauri-dev-test.mjs:24 sets both. Setting one alone gives stamps with no overlay, or an overlay that says source mapping is off (apps/desktop/client/src/lib/dev/DevInspector.tsx:108). Fixed: vite.config.ts defines import.meta.env.VITE_INSPECTOR from THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR so one flag drives both.

## Flow
- vite.config.ts: define { 'import.meta.env.VITE_INSPECTOR': JSON.stringify(process.env.THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR === '1' ? '1' : '') }
- drop VITE_INSPECTOR from scripts/dev/tauri-dev-test.mjs
- build with only THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR=1: overlay chunk present and data-loc stamped

## Expected impact
One switch for the developer inspector. Nothing user-facing changes; release builds stay free of both.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one flag for one switch
Before: 2 flags, 1 launcher setting both
After: predicted: 1 flag
Method: simulation - verifying needs a vite build, reserved to the director
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vite build with THE_TABLE_INSPECTOR=1 only: dist contains the DevInspector chunk and data-loc attributes
